column2: Having raised it with good mantras, in the lotus of power arranged, with jewels and the rest placed, one should install it in its own support.
The sacrificer, with the banner fixed, together with kin and friends, having circumambulated the abode, obtains the desired fruit.
The teacher, meditating on the Pashupata, joined with the lords of the steady mantras, should instruct the lords armed with weapons for protection.
For peace of faults of deficiency and the rest, having offered and given the offering to the quarters, the teacher should be given a fee; the sacrificer goes to heaven.
As many atoms as there are in the images, lingas and altars, so many thousands of ages the maker enjoys the fruit.
A linga that has been moved, shifted, very unevenly placed, misdirected, fallen, or fallen in the middle —
having thus established it, if it is without damage; or if it is carried off by the flow of a river and the like,
then having established another elsewhere by the rite seen in the rule, one should not move a Shiva-linga, whether well or ill placed.
With a hundred one should do installation, with a thousand the moving; joined with worship and the rest, even a worn one is well placed.
In the south or northeast one should make a pavilion with a single west-door arch; having done door worship and the rest, mantra worship on the platform,
having satisfied and worshipped the mantras and the site-deities as before, having given the directional offering outside, the teacher himself rinsing,
having fed Brahmins, should then inform Shambhu: "This is a faulty linga of Shambhu; for the peace of removing it,
by the rule of praise and the rest, preside over me, Shiva." Having thus informed the lord of gods, one should perform the peace-oblation:
with honey, ghee, milk and durva, a hundred and eight with the root-mantra. Then having established the linga one should worship it on a platform likewise.

Om, to Vyapakeshvara, ending with Nata, by the rule of Shiva and others: "Om, to the pervading heart-lord, homage; Om, to the pervading lord, to the head, homage" — the limb-mantras beginning thus; then one should have the principle dwelling there told, then the weapon:

Whatever being here angered stays dependent on the linga — leaving the linga, by Shiva's commands, let it go where it wishes.
agnipuran:103:14	He will be here joined with the lords of knowledge and ignorance. A thousand for each portion, then with the Pashupata atom,
having offered, sprinkled with peace-water and touched with kusha, one should then repeat; having given arghya in reverse order, and the principles and lords of principles,
the teacher having dismissed the lords of the eight forms stationed on the linga and pedestal, with a golden noose and with one on the bull's shoulder,
having bound with a rope and brought it, with people chanting "Shiva," the mantra-master should cast it into water; he should offer a hundred for prosperity.
For satisfaction of the guardians of the quarters and purification of the site, a hundred and a hundred; having made protection in its place, then the Mahapashupata;
the teacher should then rightly establish another linga there. One established by Asuras, sages, lineages and tantra-knowers,
whether worn or broken, one should not move even by rule. This same rule is to be applied in restoring a worn abode.
Having placed the mantra-group on a sword one should have the interior of the temple made; contraction is declared to mean death, expansion loss of wealth.
In the third, the altar of Agni, with neck, with a spotless essence; Vairaja, Pushpaka and another, Kailasa, Manika;
and Tripishtapa — only five stand on the summit of Meru. Of them the first is square, the second also oblong;
round, round-oblong, another, and the fifth eight-angled; each in nine kinds, forty-five.
The temple: first Meru, second Mandara, and Vimana, Bhadra, and Sarvatobhadra,
Charuka, Nandika, Nandi, Vardhamana, and another, Shrivatsa — these arose in the Vairajya lineage.
Balabhi, Griharaja, Shalagriha, Mandira, Vishala, Sama, Brahma-mandira, Bhuvana,
Prabhava, Shivika, Veshma — these nine arose from Pushpaka. Balaya, Dundubhi, Padma and Mahapadmaka,
Vardhani, another Ushnisha, Shankha and Kalasa, and Svavriksha — these are round, arising from Kailasa.
Gaja, Vrishabha, Hamsa, Garutman, Nrikshanayaka, Bhushana, Bhudhara, and others, Shrijaya, Prithvidhara —
these nine arose from the round-oblong called Manika. Vajra, Chakra and another, Svastika, Vajrasvastika,
Chitra, Svastikakhadga, Gada, and Shrikantha, Vijaya by name — these arose from Tripishtapa.
These are the names for cities, and these likewise for Lata and the rest; the spire rising by half the neck, broad by division;
having made the altar tenfold, the shoulder breadth by five; the neck by three; by four the Prachandaka.
Doors should be made in the directions and never in the intermediate ones. The pedestal is declared broad at the corners, ending in the middle.
In some, by a fifth part, by great, from the foot of the sanctum; their heights are double, or told otherwise.
From sixty up to a hundred fingers here; the best four doors by reduction of ten;
three are middling, then three are least. The breadth is half the height; the height exceeds in three ways,
by four, by eight, or by ten fingers; then the branches broad by a foot from the height, at its threshold.
The thickness of all is declared half the breadth; a door with two, five, seven or nine branches gives what is desired.
In a quarter of the lower branch one should place the two door-guards; one should adorn the rest of the branch with couples and foot-colored ornaments.
When pierced by a pillar there is servitude; by a tree, adversity; by a well, fear at the door; by a field, loss of wealth;
when pierced by the way of a temple, house, stone and the like there is bondage; by an assembly, no poverty; by a color, deformity;
by a mortar poverty; by a stone enmity; by shade poverty; the fault of piercing does not arise
by cutting or uprooting, or by the mark of an enclosure; by leaving twice the boundary, the fault of piercing does not arise.
The wall thick, the lower body high; the wall three times the height; the ground equal to the wall-line; the lane in many ways by division;
in the Bhadra equal with lanes, the door-lane without the front; the Shrijaya lacking behind; this Bhadra is without the sides;
the lane equal to the sanctum's thickness, or sometimes by a quarter; by half the lane the sub-lane and the rest, with one, two or three tiers.
Now I shall tell of the ordinary house, giving all desires: one-, two-, three-, four-, and eight-halled, in order.
One facing south and north; if two, then behind facing east; the four-halled facing both; of them Indra and Indra-freed;
facing Shiva, facing the water-lord's — this is Indra-faced Yama-Surya; the one in east and north called Danda; in east and south called Vata;
in west and moon called Grihavalli; the trident, it increases not; without the east hall it is a good field giving increase;
if the south is lacking it becomes Shuli; the three-halled one makes increase; the Yakshaghna lacking water, killing sons, making many enemies.

From Satyaloka; where there is no return, that is called Brahma's world. From the foot downward is Bhuloka; Bhuvah is remembered up to the sun; Svarloka and up to Bhuvah, fourteen niyutas. The egg of Brahma is a single staff, surrounded by the cosmic shell; by water, fire, air, space, then up to the origin of elements; the egg is encased tenfold, the origin of elements by the great, likewise; the remainder in tens. Having covered the great, the Pradhana stands; Ananta has no end nor does his constitution exist. That Prakriti is the cause of all, O sage, in the beginning. Countless eggs were produced there for those who see. As fire in wood, as oil in sesame, so is the Person: abiding in Pradhana, pervading, the Self of consciousness, knowing the Self. Pradhana and Purusha are the Self of all beings, by Vishnu's power in the great, wise activity, holding refuge; their separation is the cause of doubt. Mahakhya, Svatala and also Patala, O best one; black, yellow, red, white, pebble, rock and golden lands; in them and others Daityas and others dwell in comfort. Below the Patalas at the end is Shesha, Vishnu's tamasic form; Ananta bearing the earth on his head and holding other qualities; below the earth the hells lead the world, Kshatra-Vaishnava. As long as the earth is flooded by water, so long is space held. The doctrine be so. [This passage is a stray insertion from another section, noted by manuscript readings.] I shall tell the eight houses beginning with banner in the order of Indra and the rest; the washing-house, the garland-house, in fire its kitchen.
In the south the cooking and bed; in the southwest bows and weapons; wealth, the water-house, in the west; scent in the northwest;
in the north wealth and cattle one should place; in the northeast the best initiation house. A house measured by the owner's hand, with breadth, length and pedestal,
multiplied by three with the cubit, divided by eight; the remainder stands; by that up to the crow, banner and the rest;
three, wing, fire, Veda; with flavor, sage and Vasu; a house standing in the middle and at the end destroys all.
Therefore in the ninth part the dwelling is held to bring good; in its middle a pavilion is praised, equal or double in length.
In the west and water, moon and Yama, a market, row of houses; the single houses named in the directions in numbers of eight and eight;
from Ishana to Aditi; their fruits in order: fear, woman, instability, victory, growth, majesty;
dharma, quarrel and poverty at the eight east doors surely; burning, discomfort, loss of friends, loss of wealth, death, wealth;
craftsmanship and a son — the eight fruits of the south door; life, ascetic life, grain, wealth, peace, loss of purpose;
drying, enjoyment, and offspring are the fruits of the water door; disease, intoxication, pain, being chief, and wealth, life, thinness, mind;
and honor — from the north door in order.
In the east the house of Shri is told; in the southeast the kitchen; in the south the sleeping-room; in the southwest the arsenal;
in the west the dining place; in the northwest the grain store; in the north the storehouse; in the northeast the god's house.
Four-halled, three-halled, two-halled or one-halled; of the four-halled houses by difference of hall and alinda,
two hundred are born; fifty-five among them; three-halled are four; two-halled five;
one-halled four; I shall tell the one-alinda ones; twenty-eight alinda houses and towns,
by four and seven, fifty-five indeed; six-alinda twenty; by eight twenty;
eight-alinda thus; houses in a town and so on.
Those called Kimpurusha and the others, eight lands, O best one: for them accomplishment is natural, mostly happy, without effort;
no fear of old age and death; no dharma and adharma, no age-divisions; no lowest or middle, equal; from the Himalaya region at the navel.
Rishabha was born of Merudevi; from Rishabha was Bharata. Rishabha gave Shri to his son and went to Hari at Shalagrama.
From Bharata is the land Bharata; from Bharata was Sumati; Bharata, having given Lakshmi, went to Hari at Shalagrama.
That yogi — I shall tell his deeds again in the context of yoga; from Sumati, from his radiance, Indradyumna was born.
